title: Reverse a stretch of a playlist
prompt:
head is a playlist stored as a singly linked list; reverse the songs at positions left through right (1-based, inclusive) in place and return the head.

- Each node is an object with val (an integer) and next (the next node or null; None in Python). In Python, nodes are dicts: node["val"], node["next"].
- The list has 1 to 300 nodes and 1 <= left <= right <= its length.
- Relink the existing nodes in one pass with O(1) extra space.
hints: Which node's next pointer must change to point at the reversed section? It may be the head, so consider a dummy node.
Walk to before, the node at position left - 1 (the dummy if left is 1). Call start = before.next; start will end up last in the section.
Repeat right - left times: detach start.next and insert it right after before. This head-insertion reverses the section in place.

solution.explanation: A dummy node gives every section a predecessor. Each step takes the node after start and moves it to the front of the section, so after right - left moves the section is reversed and start is its last node, still linked to the rest of the list.

complexity.notes: Each of the right - left moves rewires three pointers.

followUps: Reverse the whole list recursively. What does it cost in stack space?
Check whether a list reads the same forwards and backwards in O(1) extra space.
